neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, severely disinhibited. Uses racial epithets during the examination that daughter reports are completely out of character. Laughs when told her behavior is hurtful. MMSE 20/30 — loses points on attention, recall, orientation. FAB 9/18 — severely impaired on all frontal subtests. Category fluency: 6/60 seconds. Clock drawing severely abnormal. Exhibits clear perseverative behavior — writes her name repeatedly on scratch paper.
neurological_exam.motor: Mild bilateral upper extremity rigidity. Strength 5/5.
neurological_exam.additional: Hyperorality — took food from daughter's bag unprompted during exam.

patient.chief_complaint: Two-year progressive personality change, disinhibition, and compulsive behaviors in a retired literature professor.
patient.history_present_illness: Dr. Y. is a 60-year-old right-handed Asian woman brought in by her adult daughter for progressive personality changes over 2 years. She was a highly respected literature professor known for her measured, diplomatic manner. About 2 years ago, she began making shocking remarks to students and colleagues — including using offensive language and making inappropriate personal comments in class. She was placed on administrative leave and ultimately resigned. At home, her daughter has witnessed a complete personality reversal: the formerly reserved woman now sings loudly in public, dances in grocery stores, makes sexually explicit comments to strangers, and steals small items without compunction. She has developed compulsive behaviors including collecting plastic bags, arranging household objects by color for hours, and insisting on eating rice at every meal. Her appetite is voracious — she will eat continuously until the food is removed. She has no distress about these changes and insists she is 'finally free.' No psychiatric history. No family history of dementia.

mri.impression: Severe bilateral orbitofrontal-predominant and anterior temporal atrophy with knife-blade pattern. Normal hippocampal volume. Posterior cortex preserved. Clinical correlation recommended.

advanced_imaging.impression: Severe bilateral frontotemporal hypometabolism — a pattern consistent with a frontotemporal metabolic profile. Posterior cingulate cortex and parietal metabolism preserved. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Negative — sparse-to-no amyloid neuritic plaque density. Global SUVR 0.93, below positivity threshold. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.interpretation: Opening pressure: 122 mmH2O. WBC: 1 cell/mm3 (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 38 mg/dL. Glucose: 57 mg/dL (ratio 0.66). Abeta42: 880 pg/mL (normal). Total tau: 210 pg/mL (normal). Phospho-tau 181: 36 pg/mL (normal). NfL: 2,012 pg/mL (elevated). 14-3-3: negative.

output.impression: Neuropsychological profile consistent with probable behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia. Severely impaired executive function (FAB 9/18) and social cognition (Faux Pas 3/20) with moderate retrieval-predominant memory impairment. Severe behavioral disturbance on caregiver-rated measures. Clinical correlation recommended.

warnings: SSRIs may reduce compulsive behaviors; evidence limited in FTD

output.query: bvFTD behavioral symptoms SSRI trazodone treatment evidence

results.title: SSRIs in FTD
results.finding: Modest evidence for reduction in compulsive and disinhibited behaviors with SSRIs

results.title: Trazodone in FTD
results.finding: RCT evidence for trazodone reducing agitation and sleep disturbance in FTD (Lebert 2004)

output.summary: No disease-modifying therapy exists for the frontotemporal lobar degeneration syndromes; management is symptomatic. Trazodone has randomized controlled trial evidence for reducing agitation and sleep disturbance (Lebert et al., J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 2004). SSRIs (sertraline, fluvoxamine) have modest evidence from small trials for compulsive and disinhibited behaviors. Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors have not demonstrated benefit. Clinical correlation recommended.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), probable, sporadic

differential.key_features: AD can present atypically; amyloid biomarker negativity and frontal FDG pattern argue against.
Late-life personality change without psychiatric history is rare; imaging confirms neurodegeneration.
Cardiovascular family history present but MRI shows degenerative lobar atrophy, not vascular pattern.
No urinary incontinence or gait apraxia; ventricles commensurate with atrophy.
No motor neuron signs on exam.

optimal_actions.action: Obtain brain MRI with volumetric coronal T1 to assess frontal/anterior temporal atrophy and exclude alternative structural cause
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Bilateral frontal and/or anterior temporal atrophy in a lobar pattern with relative posterior sparing

optimal_actions.action: Order metabolic dementia panel (TSH, B12, CMP, RPR/HIV per risk) to exclude reversible mimics
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No reversible metabolic or infectious cause of cognitive decline identified

optimal_actions.action: Order comprehensive neuropsychological battery characterising executive function, social cognition, language and memory
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Frontal-executive and social-cognition deficits with relative sparing of episodic memory and visuospatial function

optimal_actions.action: Search medical literature for frontotemporal dementia diagnostic criteria and management
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirms Rascovsky 2011 criteria, FDG-PET evidence (Foster 2007), and management approach (Bang 2015)

tool_parameters.query: Frontotemporal dementia diagnostic criteria and management

optimal_actions.action: Consult behavioral/cognitive neurology for syndromic diagnosis, biomarker interpretation, and longitudinal care plan
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Behavioral neurology confirms bvFTD syndrome, coordinates biomarkers and disclosure

optimal_actions.action: Order FDG-PET brain to characterise frontotemporal hypometabolism and distinguish bvFTD from AD
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Bifrontal and/or anterior temporal hypometabolism with relative posterior sparing
optimal_actions.guideline_source: Foster 2007 FDG-PET in FTD vs AD

optimal_actions.action: Order FTD genetic panel (C9orf72, GRN, MAPT) given negative family history but to exclude autosomal-dominant cause
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identifies or excludes pathogenic C9orf72 / GRN / MAPT variant relevant to prognosis and cascade testing

optimal_actions.action: Consider amyloid PET to confirm non-AD etiology if doubt remains
optimal_actions.guideline_source: Foster 2007 FDG-PET in FTD vs AD

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is non-specific in FTD; not part of the standard dementia workup unless seizures or rapidly progressive course suggest CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the cognitive workup of suspected FTD; reserved for syncope, palpitations, or pre-procedure clearance.
Echocardiography is unrelated to a neurodegenerative cognitive syndrome and adds cost without diagnostic value.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to FTD and not indicated absent syncope or palpitations.
Non-contrast head CT lacks the resolution and lobar specificity needed to characterise frontotemporal atrophy; MRI is the standard structural study.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine FTD diagnostic pathway.
Perfusion MRI is not indicated in the standard FTD workup once a structural MRI and FDG-PET (or amyloid PET) have characterised the lobar pattern.
Carotid duplex is a vascular study with no diagnostic role in primary neurodegenerative dementia.
DaTscan evaluates presynaptic dopaminergic terminals; it is not indicated unless overt parkinsonism raises concern for PD, DLB, or atypical parkinsonism (PSP/CBS overlap).

sequence_constraints.reason: Exclude structural cause of focal cognitive symptoms and screen for elevated ICP before lumbar puncture.

critical_actions: Apply Rascovsky 2011 bvFTD criteria explicitly (≥3 of 6 core features within 3 years) and document functional decline.
Assess and document decision-making, financial, and driving capacity given the high risk of impulsivity and impaired judgment in FTD.
Provide caregiver education, safety planning, and referral to FTD-focused support resources.
Offer genetic counselling and discuss cascade testing options if a pathogenic variant is identified or suspected.
contraindicated_actions: Do not start acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD and may worsen behavioral symptoms.
Do not start memantine: no evidence of benefit in bvFTD and may worsen behavioral symptoms.
Avoid antipsychotics as first-line behavioral therapy given increased cerebrovascular and mortality risk in dementia; reserve for refractory dangerous agitation with specialist oversight.
Avoid benzodiazepines for behavioral control: risk of paradoxical disinhibition and falls.
key_reasoning_points: Rascovsky bvFTD criteria met with the expected MRI and FDG pattern.
Negative amyloid biomarkers exclude AD pathology.
Mild rigidity is not a parkinsonian syndrome — DaTscan unnecessary.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Could prompt DaTscan for suspected parkinsonism.
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Mild rigidity is common in advanced bvFTD; DaTscan is not indicated.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required tools (MRI, labs, neuropsych, literature, consult) plus recommended FDG-PET / amyloid PET / genetic panel; 1–2 red herrings (mild rigidity ± family history); requires cross-modal synthesis (structural + metabolic + biomarker + neuropsych) to exclude AD and document Rascovsky criteria.
